body: فقد زين الدين زيدان، مدرب المنتخب الفرنسي، بعضًا من رصيده الشعبي في فرنسا، بعد نتائج الديوك في دوري الأمم الأوروبية. وذكر موقع فوت ميركاتو ، أن شعبية زيدان تراجعت 3 نقاط، عقب معسكره الثاني على رأس الجهاز الفني للديوك، وذلك وفقًا لاستطلاع رأي أجرته مؤسسة أودوكسا لصالح ويناماكس وإذاعة آر تي إل. ورغم هذا التراجع الطفيف، لا يزال زيدان يحظى بشعبية كبيرة لدى الفرنسيين، إذ ما زال 83% منهم، يحملون رأيًا إيجابيًا تجاه النجم السابق الذي ارتدى القميص رقم 10، وترتفع هذه النسبة إلى 90% بين محبي كرة القدم. أما فيما يتعلق بالمنتخب الفرنسي، فقد اتخذت المؤشرات اتجاهًا تنازليًا، بعدما تراجعت شعبيته 6 نقاط، لتصل إلى 69% مقابل 75% في الاستطلاع السابق. ومع ذلك، لا يزال هذا المستوى من بين أعلى المعدلات المسجلة خلال السنوات العشر الأخيرة. كما انقسمت آراء محبي كرة القدم بشأن حصيلة بداية تجربة زين الدين زيدان، على رأس الجهاز الفني لمنتخب الديوك، إذ يرى نحو نصفهم (47%) أن المنتخب الفرنسي أصبح أقل قوة، مقارنة بالفترة التي كان يقوده فيها ديدييه ديشامب، في حين يعتقد 49% أن أداء المنتخب الفرنسي، شهد تطورًا. ويبدو، وفقًا للاستطلاع، أن الحماس الذي ساد خلال معسكر شهري سبتمبر وأكتوبر بدأ يتراجع. فقد حصلت الاختيارات التكتيكية والتشكيلات، التي يعتمدها زين الدين زيدان على 74% من الآراء الإيجابية، بتراجع قدره 15 نقطة.…

Comcast shared a video of a line graph showing the massive relative spike in activity on November 19. title: The team behind Ubisoft's 'first playable AI-based R&D project' has been established as its own subsidiary called Motherbrain
summary: In the name of "more immersive and engaging player experiences," of course.
body: Use of generative AI in game dev remains as contentious as it does ubiquitous— a recent GDC report found that around 40% of devs use AI, but more than half think its influence has been negative. Ubisoft is continuing to double down on the technology , this time with Motherbrain, a new subsidiary fashioned from the team behind its "first playable generative AI experience." As reported by VGC , Motherbrain's purpose is to develop "AI for gameplay innovation, supporting all game creators in developing groundbreaking experiences … Its current focus is on new player experiences, smart NPCs with memory and AI game masters that manage large scale systemic worlds," according to an earnings report which was released Thursday. The information comes at a turbulent time for the publishing giant, which just laid off 166 employees even after Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced "outperformed expectations." A sweeping internal overhaul earlier this year saw the company reorganize its workforce into a throng of "creative houses," a decision which led to swathes of layoffs and six project cancellations, including the Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time Remake. title: I didn't realize Etsy was selling bridges now
summary: The company says its new generative AI training agreement will only be used for good. Why would anyone believe that?
body: Online marketplace Etsy, best known as a platform for selling handmade goods, recently updated its user agreement to allow itself to "develop, train, test and improve artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies" using content uploaded by sellers. This has not gone over well, with some closing their Etsy shops in protest. In response, Etsy has assured users that it doesn't plan to train AI systems designed to copy their work or replace their creativity. Instead, the company said that the change is about improving the platform and providing "services and tools that can help you run your business." body: While you can switch to first-person temporarily in Grand Theft Auto 6 when you want to get a real good close-up of a texture or when you're looking at your phone, you can't run around doing crimes and having fun like you could when GTA 5 got its first-person mode. Except actually you can, as discovered by players on Reddit and tested by our own Morgan Park. It's easy enough to activate in-game. Go to the controller settings, then under the Controller Features section change your touch pad/select button to Camera 2 / 2. Get into a car, bring up your phone with the D-pad, press Circle or B then quickly hit Select. There you go, first-person GTA 6. As Morgan's footage shows, it's completely playable. It doesn't look 100% done, however, with your shoulders clipping through the camera when you've got a longarm gun up. Seeing someone break into a car in first-person also looks a bit rough around the edges. While conspiracy theorists have convinced themselves that Rockstar is holding back this feature to sell it as DLC, I figure they're probably still polishing it to add in a future update. title: Cyberleek drops what they claim is a near-complete GTA 6 Xbox build online
summary: The leaked file is apparently around 200 GB.
body: Mysterious GTA 6 leaker Cyberleek has reemerged in the wake of GTA 6's release with another leak: This time, they have released what they claim to be a near-complete build of GTA 6 on Xbox from November 2026. In their post, Cyberleek says they'll drop the one file they've withheld—the main executable—if their crypto coin reaches a $15 million market cap. Yeah, we're doing this again. Comments on a now-removed Reddit post say the leaked file is around 200 GB, which is close to the size of GTA 6 on consoles. Cyberleek says they will release the exe on November 23, no matter what. "It is an Xbox build this time, not a PC build. CL does not care. This community will have it emulated inside a week, running far past 30fps. CL told you not to preorder for a reason. This is one of the reasons," the posts read. "If the Xbox build cannot be made to work and support holds, CL will work to get a PS5 build—a fallback, most likely never required. Either way: the Xbox build is going out. No double dipping for Take-Two/Rockstar." title: Help: I can't stop obeying traffic laws in GTA 6
summary: What's happening to me!?
body: A few minutes into my first play session with Grand Theft Auto 6, I was doing my first bit of driving. I'd been cruising down the Leonida Keys, and as I was patiently waiting at a red light and humming along with the radio, I had a sudden realization: I was patiently waiting at a red light. I immediately floored it, weaving into and out of oncoming traffic and channeling all the years of training in being a vehicular menace I'd been provided by prior Grands Theft Auto. But just a short way down the road, moments after blasting past a few panicked pedestrians I'd aggressively robbed of the right of way, it happened again: Without thinking, I'd come to a complete stop at a stop sign. I'm playing the world's most renowned automotive crime fantasy, and I can't stop observing the basic tenets of road safety. (Image credit: Rockstar) Repeatedly across the hours I've put into GTA 6 since launch, I've been succumbing to an embarrassing habit of obeying driverly etiquette. I'm following other drivers at a reasonable distance when I could be forcing them off the road to save time. title: GTA 6 has the best use of the PS5 controller I've ever seen
summary: The PS5 triggers are changing how I drive in GTA.
body: Six years into owning my PS5, I can count on one hand how many times the DualSense controller's resistive triggers have proved essential to the game I'm playing. They're key for Astro Bot's varied trigger-based mechanics, of course, and I wouldn't want to play Death Stranding 2 without my heavy backpack fighting back against me. But my new favorite use of the PS5 controller is GTA 6. GTA 6 uses the whole DualSense buffalo for a variety of sensory additives—I can feel it in the haptics when I roll over the rumble strip on the shoulders of roads or rear end another car—but the way it uses the triggers is especially effective. The resistive triggers activate when you'd expect, like while shooting guns, but they also come into play in activities that feel like they were designed around the controller: When swinging dumbbells, for instance, the triggers help me time when to release and start another rep. It's cool stuff. Rockstar's smartest use of the triggers, and one of my favorite new features of GTA 6 in general, is its two-stage throttle for vehicles : When you pull the throttle (right trigger) in any car, there's a hard resistive stop at about the 50% to 60% point. title: Don't stress about collectathon completionism in Queen's Domain: It eventually gives you tools to help find hidden treasures
summary: Collect 'em all, eventually.
body: Queen's Domain has, by my count, four categories of collectible you have to hoover up if you want to see its more hidden endings, and some of them are real bastards to find⁠—I'd resigned myself to queueing up guides on YouTube to get it all done. Guides are great, you might still need them for some of the collectibles, and if there's one game that feels like it was designed with Google/Reddit/forum help in mind, it's Queen's Domain. But I was thrilled to discover that, very late in the game, Queen's Domain provides a waypoint tool to guide you to its hidden collectibles. It turned what I worried would be a tedious process into yet another example of this game's boundless capacity for surprise and discovery. I know I would have appreciated the heads-up, the permission to not worry about finding them all earlier in my playtime. If that's how you felt, and you aren't looking for spoilers, great: You can stop reading here. title: GTA 5's Steam concurrents have gone up rather than down now that GTA 6 is out, suggesting a lot of PC players are waiting
summary: We have GTA 6 at home.
body: Pour one out for the PC gamers who are now forced to watch everyone frolic in the streets of Grand Theft Auto 6 on consoles this week. The next best thing on PC is GTA 5, and its recent Steam concurrents suggest people are trying their best to fight the FOMO until Rockstar decides to bring the new one over. You might assume GTA 5 player counts would tank now that it's old news, but the numbers have actually jumped up a bit in the last month. SteamDB shows a peak of around 87,000 concurrent players in the last day, an almost 10% increase from October. There's been a bit of a dip today—which could partially be attributed to GTA 6 finally becoming available in every region—but it's not as sharp of a drop as you'd think it'd be for a 13-year-old game. In fact, GTA 5 has steadily kept a good amount of players over the last year, with major spikes happening around the occasional price discount. It usually hovers around 40,000 to 50,000 average concurrent players, and GTA 6's release hasn't broken the pattern. title: Should you give the statue to Benedict Halifax in GTA 6?
summary: In the Chapter 3 mission Dubious Provenance, should you trust, or not trust, the eccentric antiques dealer?
body: Deciding whether to give the statue to Benedict Halifax is a decision you'll need to make during the fourth story mission of Chapter 3 in GTA 6 , called Dubious Provenance. This mission will kick off after Cal visits the Bayside apartment you're borrowing from Boobie to inspect the hard drive. Once Cal leaves, you'll see an icon of a statuette at the closet door. Remember, you didn't just acquire a hard drive but a bronze statuette in Chapter 1, and if you interact with it now the mission will begin. First, you need to drive to Capri, a ritzy town on the other side of the map. At the antiques store, Evelyn Andrews tells you she isn't interested in the obviously stolen item, but art dealer Benedict Halifax approaches you on the sly and says he can have it appraised for you. Should you give the statue to him? Give the statue to Halifax : He'll give you a watch to hold onto as collateral while he appraises the statue. Then he'll vanish for a while, trying to duck you, and you'll have to call him repeatedly to track him down again.
